headline: Highest risk is data leakage: kotaemon handles API keys and broad network egress while taipy is network-isolated, but the pairwise interaction is otherwise mostly docs-only and low-confidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A plausible injection path exists if kotaemon’s web UI content is copied into taipy workflows, but no shared channel is documented. kotaemon ingests HTML/MHTML and chat transcripts; taipy has no IO surfaces shown, so the bridge is indirect and likely manual. This is lower severity because the pathway is unusual and not evidenced as default.
conditions: IF an operator copies kotaemon-generated or web-derived text into taipy inputs without review, prompt injection can propagate.
IF taipy is configured to execute instructions embedded in imported text, the bridge becomes exploitable.
mitigations: Require manual review before moving text from kotaemon to taipy.
Strip instructions from imported documents and transcripts.
Use a fixed schema for taipy inputs instead of free text.
Log source provenance for any copied content.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance checks between the tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon touches API keys and broad document types and can egress to external model APIs; taipy shows no egress and no data classes, so the main leakage risk is one-way from kotaemon to third parties rather than between the pair. The pairwise risk exists in default use if sensitive files are processed in kotaemon, but taipy itself is not documented as a leak source.
conditions: IF sensitive documents or API keys are loaded into kotaemon, they may be transmitted to external APIs.
IF taipy is later fed kotaemon outputs containing sensitive excerpts, those excerpts can be re-exposed in downstream artifacts.
mitigations: Avoid loading secrets into kotaemon unless strictly necessary.
Disable external API providers in kotaemon where possible.
Redact API keys before document ingestion.
Keep taipy inputs limited to non-sensitive summaries.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before any outbound API call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents are open-source and runnable in principle, but the profiles do not show overlapping write surfaces or shared mutable resources. kotaemon writes to ./ktem_app_data and taipy exposes no filesystem or network write capability here, so a direct conflict is not evidenced. Uncertainty remains, but the safer choice is low rather than none because taipy’s missing surfaces are undocumented, not impossible.
conditions: IF taipy is deployed with a writable shared directory matching kotaemon’s ./ktem_app_data, write contention can occur.
IF both are given the same external mutable resource through orchestration, conflicts become possible.
mitigations: Place each agent in its own working directory.
Avoid sharing writable volumes between the agents.
Run only one writer per resource at a time.
Document ownership of any shared files.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon is a RAG/chat system that can generate citations and answers, and taipy is a data-engineering/automation tool that may consume outputs as workflow inputs. No verification step is documented between them, so if taipy treats kotaemon output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream artifacts. The interaction is inferred from profiles, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF taipy ingests kotaemon-generated answers or citations without validation, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF taipy triggers automated data-processing steps from those outputs, the error blast radius expands.
mitigations: Require human review of kotaemon outputs before taipy uses them.
Validate citations and source links independently.
Use taipy only on structured, machine-checked fields.
Add a rejection rule for uncited claims.
requires-engineering: implement automated fact-checking or provenance verification.

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and chat transcripts, which can create compliance obligations, while taipy’s profile shows no touched data classes or residency constraints. No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so the compliance risk is limited to gaps in kotaemon’s handling rather than a proven pairwise violation.
conditions: IF kotaemon processes regulated data and sends it to external APIs, policy obligations may be triggered.
IF taipy stores or republishes kotaemon outputs under a different retention policy, a mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to kotaemon.
Do not route regulated data to external APIs without approval.
Set a retention policy for taipy outputs.
Keep audit logs for sensitive workflows.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems.
